Increase the carve depth enough to read across views while preserving a single dominant mass.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent compact mass in all four views, so it avoids the worst fragmentation failure. The notch/cut creates a recognizable dominant gesture and keeps the form from becoming a pure box, but the public void is still shallow and reads more as a cut than a genuinely inhabited court or terrace. The blue access edge is acknowledged only weakly; there is no strong ground-level opening or legible public threshold aligned to that frontage, so the neighborhood-living brief is only partially supported. The silhouette is serviceable but not especially resolved as a program-bearing section; it feels more like a generic rectilinear slab with a small subtraction than a calibrated street building. Reference 1 supports the idea of a strong single mass with a clear upper articulation; reference 2 supports a carved public figure/courtyard; reference 3 supports active street-edge grounding.
